newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 31.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.
- The Irish government has sent out the strongest signals yet that it is preparing for a summer election.
- Irish publicans have been warned that beer prices will be fixed at last year's levels if they do not immediately reverse the latest five pence increase in the cost of a pint of beer.
- Nursing union leaders are to meet health service managers on Friday to try to resolve differences over the level of cover to be provided in the event of a strike.

- The Irish Deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring is to press the British government to investigate new evidence of the military's role in Bloody Sunday when he meets the Northern Secretary Sir Patrick Mayhew next week.
- Ireland's state run Telecom Eireann hopes to be able to invest around 100 million Irish pounds in overseas opportunities within three years, its chief executive, Alfie Kane said on Thursday.
- Hospitals have started cancelling appointments, admissions and operations in preparation for the nurses' strike threatened on Monday week.
- Irish police investigating a major drugs cartel with international links were questioning three businessmen on Thursday night.

- The Partnership 2000 pay deal was voted through at Thursday's special ICTU delegate conference by a majority of 83 votes despite serious concern expressed over both the two percent local bargaining rise and union recognition.
- AIB is set to join the elite group of "AA' rated banks after a statement by rating agency Moody's that it was reviewing the group and its subsidiaries for possible upgrade.
- Ireland's opposition Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern has moved to strengthen his general election team, following the dramatic resignation by Maire Geoghegan-Quinn.

- Over 10,000 Irish pounds worth of pornographic books, magazines, videos and sex aids were seized by Irish police after a raid on a County Cork farm at the centre of the deliberate BSE infection probe.
- An Irish government proposal to extend cabinet confidentiality to civil servants in certain cases was sharply criticised by opposition parliamentarians on Thursday.
